title: GAIA script capability manifest
description: Constrains .gaia/script-capabilities.json: the one declaration of what each script named in .claude/settings.json's permissions.allow actually reaches for (network, github-write, git-write, fs-write, tmp, invokes). A malformed edit fails this cheap structural validation before check-script-capabilities.sh runs its semantic reconciliation against the script's real closure.

script.description: Repo-relative path to the allowlisted script (never a leading /). Unique across the manifest; a second entry naming the same script is a DUPLICATE finding, not a silent last-wins.

capabilities.description: The script's declared reach, as vocabulary terms. An empty array is legal and meaningful: a pure script that reaches for none of the six terms declares nothing. The reconciling check's declared-but-unreached direction (a SURPLUS finding) is what keeps an empty array honest rather than a place to hide unused permission.

why.description: Plain-language reason this script's declared capabilities are its whole reach: what the script does and why these terms, and no others, cover it.

maintainer_only.description: Whether this script is withheld from the shipped release. Required on every entry (an absent key is never treated as false) and reconciled against .gaia/release-exclude in GAIA's own tree only, since .gaia/release-exclude is itself release-excluded and unavailable to an adopter checkout.

waiver.description: A waiver suppresses both reconciliation directions (an UNDECLARED finding and a SURPLUS finding) for exactly one script-capability pair, and suppresses no other finding class: UNRESOLVED, BAD-TERM, BAD-GRANT, NO-ENTRY, ORPHAN, DUPLICATE, and MARKING are never waivable. A waived pair still prints its WAIVER line on every run, passing or failing.

why.description: Plain-language reason this one capability is waived for this one script.

capabilityTerm.description: One of six vocabulary terms: network (any outbound call), github-write (an authenticated mutating gh verb), git-write (a commit, tag, or branch mutation), fs-write:<glob> (a write, described by a repo-relative glob), tmp (a write into the system temporary directory), invokes:<path> (a call into another script, sourced or executed). JSON Schema draft 2020-12 forbids lookahead, so two rules are checker-side assertions rather than schema-enforceable: an invokes: target carries no .. segment and names a file that exists, and an fs-write: glob is repo-relative and well-formed (no leading / or ~, no .. segment).
